title: 第23章 橡木酒馆第24章 琉璃川千代的早晨
slug: 落魄贵族千金被迫成为我的女仆
lines: ：枫叶城的酒馆是二十四小时不打烊的，这始于十年前现任伯爵大人继承爵位后的改革。
那就是取消宵禁。
自那时起，虽然夜间枫叶城的大门还是会关闭不允许进出，但城内的各处酒馆旅店都不用在夜间关门，可以二十四小时营业了。
据说这是伯爵大人为了促进领地内商业繁荣所作出的改变。
酒保米勒不太懂这些改革，他只知道从那时起，那黑心老板就时不时的让他在酒馆值完白班又值夜班。
虽然说能够多挣两个铜币的夜班费，但已经劳累了一整天的米勒更想回家美美的睡上一觉，而不是在酒馆内强撑着眼皮服务这些个酒鬼。
此时，外面的天空已经蒙蒙亮了。
米勒强撑着眼皮，无精打采的用双肘撑着吧台，要不是担心老板来了之后发现他偷懒扣工资，米勒此时真想直接躺地上睡觉。
没有床垫和被子也没关系，就他现在这状态，差点站着都能睡着了。
酒吧里此时没什么动静，只有几个稀稀拉拉已经喝醉的酒鬼趴在桌上鼾声如雷。
米勒也没去管他们，反正酒钱早就付过了。
就在这时，原本只有寒风灌入的酒馆门口传来了脚步声。
米勒一脸困惑的抬眼看去，谁家好人大清早来酒馆啊。
难不成是巴克大师那个酒蒙子？
可他不是去那什么蒸汽工厂了么，来回一趟得十几里路吧，要说有谁大清早就要喝酒，那米勒只能想到他。
但出现的人并不是米勒想象中的那位巴克大师，而是另一位熟人。
“杰克？”
“你怎么一大清早来城里了。”
米勒十分意外的看着杰克，这是他的老熟人了，他们都是枫叶城边上松风镇的居民。
不仅如此，他们俩还是邻居呢。
杰克一脸无奈的走到吧台前，将一根木棍放在边上，行李也是直接甩在了地上。
他一屁股坐到吧台前的高脚凳上：“还不是因为领主大人的召集令，我被征召了。”
“昨天晚上连夜就有人来敲门通知我了。”
米勒抬头看了看墙上的时钟，这才六点半：“那也没必要来那么早吧，这会城门也才刚开没多久吧。”
枫叶城的主城大门在日落之后就关了，不允许平常人进出，直到早上天亮时分才会再次打开。
而且一般来说，通知到本人之后都会给对方一点时间来准备和赶路。
毕竟这年头也没什么交通工具，运气好可能可以遇上商队，花点钱可以搭个便车。
运气要是不好或者说不愿意花钱，那就只能全凭两条腿在那里走了。
“嗨，这你就不懂了吧。”
杰克脸上露出了一丝高深莫测：“昨晚来宣布召集令的人说了，这服役期是按报到时间算的，每天早上九点前报到的人，当天就给算服役一天。”
“我这早点来，不就能多混一天服役期么。”
“等真到了出征的时候，指不定就到了给工钱的时间点了。”
服役期只有四十天，超期就得按天给钱。
这条帝国律法百年来一直都没变过。
就算是贵族，违反了帝国法律也要被帝国裁判所处罚。
底层的这些自由民虽然没什么见识，但对于这些事关自身利益的事情那是摸得门清。
content_en:
: The tavern in Maple Leaf City is open 24 hours a day. This started from the reform after the current Earl inherited the title ten years ago.
That is to lift the curfew.
Since then, although the gates of Maple Leaf City will still be closed at night and no entry or exit is allowed, the taverns and hotels in the city no longer need to close at night and can be open 24 hours a day.
It is said that this is a change made by the earl in order to promote the prosperity of business in the territory.
The bartender Miller didn't understand much about these reforms. He only knew that since then, the sinister boss had made him work in the pub after the day shift and the night shift from time to time.
Although he could earn two extra copper coins for the night shift, Miller, who had been working hard all day, wanted to go home and have a good night's sleep instead of serving these drunkards with his eyes open in the tavern.
At this time, the sky outside was already bright.
Miller held up his eyelids and rested his elbows on the bar listlessly. If he hadn't been worried that the boss would find out that he was lazy and deducted his salary when he arrived, Miller would have really wanted to lie down on the floor and sleep.
It didn't matter if he didn't have a mattress or quilt. In his current state, he could almost fall asleep standing up.
There was not much movement in the bar at this time, except for a few drunkards lying on the table and snoring loudly.
Miller didn't care about them, since the wine had already been paid for anyway.
At this moment, footsteps came from the door of the tavern, where only the cold wind had entered.
Miller looked up with a confused look on his face. Who is this nice guy coming to the pub so early in the morning?
Could it be that Master Buck's drunkard?
But wasn't he going to that steam factory? The round trip was more than ten miles away. If anyone wanted to drink early in the morning, Miller could only think of him.
But the person who appeared was not the Master Buck that Miller imagined, but another acquaintance.
"Jack?"
"Why did you come to the city so early in the morning?"
Miller looked at Jack in surprise. This was an old acquaintance of his. They were both residents of Songfeng Town on the edge of Maple Leaf City.
Not only that, they are neighbors.
Jack walked to the bar with a helpless expression, placed a wooden stick beside it, and threw his luggage directly on the ground.
He sat down on the high stool in front of the bar: "I was not recruited because of the Lord's summons order."
"Last night, someone knocked on the door to notify me."
Miller looked up at the clock on the wall. It was only half past six: "There's no need to come so early. The city gate has just opened not long ago."
The main gate of Maple Leaf City is closed after sunset, and ordinary people are not allowed to enter or exit. It will not be opened again until dawn in the morning.
And generally speaking, after notifying the person, the other party will be given some time to prepare and go on their way.
After all, there is no transportation these days. If you are lucky, you may encounter a caravan and pay a little money to hitch a ride.
If you are unlucky or unwilling to spend money, you can only rely on your own two legs to get there.
"Hey, you don't understand this."
There was a trace of incomprehension on Jack's face: "The person who came to announce the call-up order last night said that the service period is calculated based on the reporting time. Those who report before nine o'clock every morning will be counted as serving for one day that day."
"If I come earlier, can't I get one more day of service?"
"When it's time to go on an expedition, it might be time to pay wages."
The service period is only forty days, and if you exceed the period of service, you will have to pay on a daily basis.
This imperial law has not changed for hundreds of years.
Even nobles will be punished by the imperial tribunal if they violate imperial laws.
Although these free people at the bottom have little knowledge, they are very knowledgeable about matters related to their own interests.
